conclusion: All meaningful optimization avenues are exhausted for the Bifrost-1 decoder benchmark.

best_result.description: Fused QKV both branches, mlp op for flattened image MLP, scores-only attention flattening, prefix caching of text branch, split residual architecture

graph_optimizations.dual_branch_slice: Done — text/image separate paths via slice
graph_optimizations.prefix_caching: Done — all text computations cached per prompt
graph_optimizations.weight_fusion: Done — QKV fused both branches (verified optimal vs split)
graph_optimizations.flattened_linears: Done — M=512 for QKV/O/MLP (verified better cuBLAS)
graph_optimizations.node_count_minimization: Done — 65 nodes, diminishing returns below that

inductor_compilation.safe_ops: reshape, transpose, slice, add, mul, silu, scale, concat, repeat_heads
inductor_compilation.unsafe_ops: linear, matmul, rms_norm, softmax, cast (bf16 reduction precision mismatch)
inductor_compilation.reason: Heavy compute ops (linear/matmul) can't be compiled (precision mismatch). Remaining view/elementwise ops don't benefit enough from fusion to offset region boundary overhead. Small regions = net negative. Full region = quality failure (~77% raw speedup but 8.7% RMSE).

failed_approaches: K flattening at M=256 (tile boundary quality failure)
MLP gate+up weight fusion (100M element budget exceeded)
Scale folding into Q weights (bf16 rounding quality failure)
6 Inductor regions with mlp op (2.2% slower)

practical_ceiling: ~72-73% speedup on A100 with bf16 fp32-accumulation matmuls
theoretical_ceiling: ~77-80% if bf16 reduction precision were acceptable (quality fails)
